changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious place because cards, formatting and data access are each funnelled through a single module; a few small duplicated expressions keep it from a clean 5.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:1 — routes depend only on data.ts, which alone depends on api.ts; templates depend on partials.ts; clean one-way layering
app/src/client/fragments.ts:5 — client islands re-fetch server-rendered HTML instead of duplicating templates, so server and client share markup by construction, not by copy

app/src/routes/(home).ts:80 — implicit string contract: the id `results` must match the selector in app/src/client/pokemon-browser.ts:50 (same for `move-tables`: app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:272 vs app/src/client/moves-panel.ts:22)

coupling.rationale: Loose coupling with clear seams (server renders, islands enhance); the weaknesses are soft string contracts between templates and client code and a build-render convention every route must opt into.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:174-198 — cardsForPokemon<T> is parameterised by the real variation (a ref extractor plus an extra-mapper), reused verbatim by the move, ability and type pages without copying

app/src/components/partials.ts:55-57 — cardList is the single card-list renderer; team ordering is correctly a separate teamCard path, so adding name-sort to cardList covers every dex-ordered list in one edit
app/src/components/partials.ts:19-19 — Card's optional `types`/`hidden` fields show mild flag creep carrying ability-specific concerns into the general card shape

app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:39-53 — each route repeats the same defineRoute + 404 + document-title boilerplate (6 files) rather than a small resource-route factory, so an Items section means copying that skeleton
abstraction_design.rationale: The helpers (format, cards, api cache, section/count partials) stretch to similar cases without flags or copying; the per-route handler/document/404 boilerplate is the main thing you'd duplicate for a new resource.

findings.issue: catch-all try/catch in member() swallows every error (API outages, refactors, typos) and silently drops a team member from the page
findings.suggestion: Catch narrowly (e.g. only the 404 path via api's null result) and let real failures surface or be logged

findings.issue: Client islands locate server markup by hardcoded selector strings (`#results`, `#move-tables`), so renaming an id in a template silently breaks the island
findings.suggestion: Share selector/element-id constants between the route templates and the client modules

findings.issue: The `labels.get(x.name) ?? humanize(x.name)` badge-label fallback is duplicated in four files
findings.suggestion: Add a typeBadge(ref, labels) helper next to getTypeLabels in data.ts

findings.issue: isBuildRender must be remembered in every route handler; a new route that forgets it fetches the live API during Gracile's build-render pass
findings.suggestion: Wrap handlers in a small helper (or centralise the guard in data.ts) so the convention is enforced in one place

findings.issue: getSpecies inlines the same validation regex that validName defines at data.ts:351
findings.suggestion: Hoist validName above getSpecies and reuse it

findings.issue: The moveTables template helper is exported from the route file though only used there, and is inconsistent with the other shared fragments living in components/partials.ts
findings.suggestion: Drop the export, or move the helper to components/partials.ts where the other template fragments live

findings.issue: A single 593-line global stylesheet means every page's style change touches one shared file
findings.suggestion: Acceptable at this size; if it grows, split per-route CSS files imported by the document

findings.issue: All five islands are imported eagerly into the single client entry, so each new island grows the bundle every page loads
findings.suggestion: Fine while islands are tiny; consider per-route client entries if more are added

summary: This is a cleanly layered small app: routes compose shared data/format/partial helpers, all Pokémon cards render through one template with one sprite path, and the API base URL, cache and concurrency rules live in a single module. Removing or adding a resource touches only its route file plus one or two helpers, and the client islands reuse server markup via fragment fetching instead of duplicating logic. The deductions are soft, not structural: duplicated label-fallback expressions, hardcoded selector contracts between templates and islands, a build-render guard every handler must remember, and per-route 404 boilerplate that a new resource section would copy.
